Supermarkets Across Europe Hit by New Fridge Cyberattacks
Publication: Nov. 2, 2026, 6:56 AM EST / Updated Nov. 2, 2026, 10:01 AM EST. Authors: Yuliya Talmazan and Reuters

Multiple European supermarket chains experienced coordinated cyberattacks on their refrigeration systems Monday, affecting stores across Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Estonia. The incidents caused temperature spikes and food spoilage at numerous locations.

Affected: Sweden: ICA stores, including ICA Kvantum in Sjöbo; Coop (six stores affected). Netherlands: Ahold Delhaize chain. Belgium: Colruyt Group (Spar stores, five shops hit); Carrefour (15 of 700+ stores). Ireland: Musgrave SuperValu stores (13 locations). Estonia: One client of a refrigeration technology company. Luxembourg: mentioned but no specific retailers named.

Hackers accessed refrigeration control systems and switched evaporators to defrost mode, raising temperatures to approximately 122 degrees Fahrenheit. The Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel CEO confirmed the cyberattack methodology.

This follows a similar cyberattack in France last month where hackers compromised hundreds of supermarket cooling units. The European Commission stated the incident demonstrates "how digital threats can increasingly affect citizens' everyday lives." Sweden's cybersecurity center acknowledged exposure of "quite a lot of exposed operational technology devices" requiring updates.

ICA told NBC News its systems were not affected, but that it had been informed of "an incident at a small number of stores that use an external supplier and have their connectivity outside ICA's central network."

No claims of responsibility were made, and authorities have not publicly identified perpetrators. The incidents occur amid broader European security concerns stemming from Russia's war in Ukraine.
